full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J : This First Appeal is directed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014 (decree signed on 30- 10-2014) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Money Sail No. 79 of 2013 rejecting the plaint. 

 4. The trial Court after hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014 rejected the plaint. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014, the plaintiff-appellants preferred this appeal. 

 9. Mr. Bikash Paul, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent No. 7, on the other hand, supports the Impugned judgment and decree and contends that the learned Joint District Judge was perfectly y justified in allowing the prayer for rejection of the plaint on the clear finding that the plaintiffs without referring the dispute to arbitration as per Clause 25 of the agreement filed the suit and earlier the plaintiffs on the similar type dispute filed writ petition and as per direction given in the writ petition the defendants paid all outstanding dues to the plaintiffs. He further submits that the contents of clause 25 of the agreement clearly disclosed that all disputes including financial matter should be referred to arbitration and in that view of the matter the plaintiffs ought to have referred the dispute to arbitration as per clause 25 of the agreement before filing of the instant suit. He further submits that the defendants as per direction given in writ petition paid entire outstanding dues to the plaintiffs and in that view of the matter ultimate result of this money suit is as clear as day light, such a suit should be buried at its inception so that no further time is consumed in a fruitless litigation. Mr. Bikash Paul to strengthen his submissions has relied on the decisions reported in 45 DLR (AD) 31, 11 BLD 315, 10 BLT 39, 11 BLD 312, 43 DLR 242, 53 DLR(AD) 12 and 55 DLR 211. 

 10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the plaint of the suit along with other materials on record including the agreement Between the parties as well as the impugned judgment and decree. 

 20. It is indeed unfortunate that the learned joint district judge did not at all consider all these aspects of the case both on law and fact in deciding an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint and non-consideration of the same has caused a great miscarriage of justice. We are therefore of the opinion that the judgment and decree of the joint district judge is totally unsatisfactory and the same suffers from various error. 

 23. In the result the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014 (decree signed on 30-10-2014) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Money Suit No. 79 of 2013 rejecting the plaint is set-aside. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka is, however, directed to proceed with the suit expeditiously in accordance with law.
